scope: Repository traceability graph linking findings, canonical tasks, decisions, claims, and evidence paths.

nodes.label: Runs execute as detached asynchronous work inside the web process.
Approval continuation is held in memory and cannot safely resume after restart.
The product has deterministic simulation and a local Ollama-compatible provider path.
Skills are loaded from database versions; repository skill files are not automatically imported.
There is no explicit governed semantic or episodic memory contract.
The planner requests a short plan and the runner executes ready steps sequentially in one process.
Tools run in the application process and do not have a general filesystem, network, CPU, memory, or syscall sandbox.
The current distribution uses SQLite and assumes a single-writer deployment.
The repository lacks a model registry that records model hashes, provenance, license, quantization, capabilities, and evaluation results.
The repository lacks a versioned knowledge ingestion and citation provenance subsystem.
Authentication exists, but tenant isolation, resource ownership, service identity, and delegated agent identity are not expressed as a complete authorization model.
Token counts and run events exist, but end-to-end traces, SLOs, quality metrics, resource accounting, and per-tool budgets are absent.
A public free tier is not guaranteed to remain free, keyless, private, available, or sovereign.
MCP standardizes host-client-server integration for tools, resources, prompts, capability negotiation, progress, cancellation, errors, logging, authorization, and user consent.
A2A defines agent discovery, task lifecycle, streaming, artifacts, idempotency, versioning, and security for cross-agent interoperability.

OWASP identifies prompt injection, data disclosure, supply-chain compromise, poisoning, improper output handling, excessive agency, prompt leakage, vector weaknesses, misinformation, and unbounded consumption as major LLM application risks.
SLSA, SPDX, and CycloneDX provide complementary provenance and bill-of-materials mechanisms for software, models, datasets, and builds.
W3C PROV models entities, activities, agents, derivations, versions, and reproducibility.
Selective governed memory may improve long-horizon consistency while reducing repeated context.
Role-separated planner, builder, verifier, and red-team loops may improve reliability for complex tasks but can increase latency and token use.
Adaptive reasoning depth and model routing can outperform one-model-for-all execution at equal cost or latency.
Context selection quality may deliver more value than simply increasing context-window size.
A local SQL metadata baseline plus optional retrieval adapters is safer than early commitment to a vector or graph vendor.
Energy claims should use workload-defined full-system measurements or clearly labeled proxies, not unsupported per-query estimates.
OpenTelemetry provides a portable basis for traces, metrics, logs, and emerging generative-AI semantic conventions.
Policy engines can separate policy decision from enforcement, but adopting an external engine adds operational and language complexity.
WASI, container sandboxes, and microVMs represent different isolation-cost points and no single boundary fits all deployments.
Workload identity and stronger authentication patterns exist for distributed systems, but are unnecessary overhead for a single-node local baseline.
A model and dataset bill of materials can improve reproducibility, license compliance, vulnerability response, and rollback.
A system cannot be called sovereign if the user cannot export, inspect, delete, restore, and migrate its data and operational state.
Durable execution can be built internally for the local baseline or delegated to a workflow engine for larger deployments.
Automatic agent self-modification without evaluation, rollback, and approval can amplify regressions and compromise.
Memory, retrieval, tools, and agents create cross-tenant and cross-run leakage paths beyond conventional request authorization.
A small set of deterministic, high-value domain evaluations is more actionable than a large generic benchmark suite.
Model quality, license, hardware fit, and safety can change across model revisions and quantizations.
Cache layers can reduce latency and cost but may serve stale, sensitive, or policy-incompatible outputs.
Human approval is not meaningful if the interface hides the actor, data, tool, arguments, side effects, uncertainty, or rollback path.
Competitive advantage is more likely to come from trusted execution, local autonomy, domain workflows, and measurable improvement than from a larger list of model providers.
Observability data can itself leak prompts, secrets, personal data, and proprietary artifacts.
Offline-first operation benefits from append-only events, deterministic replay, conflict rules, and explicit synchronization rather than ad hoc database copying.
Prometheus metrics are designed for operational monitoring and are not an exact per-request accounting ledger.
Structured error taxonomies improve agent recovery more reliably than natural-language error messages alone.
The raw outputs of earlier interactive deep-research sessions were not present as files in the supplied repository.
The original package contained a second language catalog and language-specific tests.
Task-specific context packs can reduce instruction conflict and context waste compared with loading the full research corpus into every agent run.
Run, step, and approval status mutations in the runner are guarded by a pure lifecycle transition model.
The evidence reducer detects event-sequence gaps, unresolved tool calls, unresolved approvals, conflicting terminal events, and completed runs lacking step-completion evidence.
The deterministic v7 baseline evaluation executed eight cases and all eight passed in the audit environment.

The v9 portable durable core defines revisioned checkpoints, expiring leases, bounded worker passes, deterministic side-effect receipts, fail-closed reconciliation, encrypted backup, and independent proof verification without a native database dependency.

The v9 durable proof injected a crash after one external side effect and before checkpoint persistence; a replacement worker completed the job with two attempts while the side-effect counter remained one, then restored the encrypted snapshot and passed independent verification.

The v10 schema and migrations define user-scoped run idempotency, durable jobs, side-effect receipts, a transactional outbox, approval expiry, ownership fields, audit redactions, and governed memory tables.
Run creation, run-event sequence allocation, and audit-chain append use immediate SQLite transactions; event and audit writes create outbox records in the same transaction.
Three SQL migrations applied successfully to an in-memory SQLite database and passed required-column, index, and foreign-key validation using Node built-in SQLite.
The encrypted application backup tests restored a clean SQLite target, rejected a wrong passphrase and a tampered archive, and refused an unauthorized overwrite.

The governed memory baseline implements owner isolation, provenance, sensitivity, correction links, expiry, deletion, content hashes, reasoned scoring, and token-budgeted retrieval, with automatic agent injection disabled.

User export and account deletion now include owned application data, exclude provider secret ciphertext from export, cascade owner data, and apply logical audit redaction overlays while preserving raw hash-chain verification.

The v10 release generates a CycloneDX SBOM, license inventory, model inventory, and source-tree provenance while excluding secrets, dependencies, build output, databases, and caches from release archives.
The constrained environment could not fetch or rebuild the better-sqlite3 native binding and therefore could not execute the native database integration suites.
Durable leases now include monotonically increasing fencing tokens and every lease-bound mutation rejects stale tokens, including when a worker identity is reused.
The step-level durable workflow recovered after an injected crash following an idempotent step and completed without executing the completed step twice.
Approval decisions now carry a persisted revision and use a status-and-revision compare-and-set update, while stale clients receive an explicit conflict.

Verification attestations bind requirement revision, task revision, source tree hash, test output hash, optional artifact hash, release candidate hash, builder, verifier, status, and limitations into an integrity hash.

Generated property probes accepted 300 acyclic graphs, rejected their injected cycles, preserved routing decisions across 200 permutations, allowed one winner among 20 lease claimants, and rejected a stale fenced completion.
Targeted semantic mutation probes killed six deliberately weakened variants covering ownership, memory injection, model health, dry-run side effects, dependency cycles, and approval revisions.
The model router now records verification quality and health state, rejects unavailable models, and applies task-class weighting for verification work.
Risk-adjusted autonomy denies dry-run side effects and prompt-derived authority, and requires human control for high-risk, external, irreversible, or reconciliation-prone operations.
Governed-memory ablation tests distinguish raw semantic retrieval from governed retrieval and exclude high-similarity instruction-like or encoded malicious memories.
The operator interface now separates runtime metrics from pilot evidence, treats unknown release evidence as blocking, and exposes immutable verification records as a distinct control plane.
